For $Y=Y^i\partial _i$ on $\mathbb R^n$ and $v=v^i\partial _i|_p$, the Euclidean directional derivative is \[ ar abla _vY=v(Y^i)\partial _i|_p, \qquad v(Y^i)=v^j rac{\partial Y^i(p)}{\partial x^j}. \] For a vector field $X$, this gives egin{equation} ar abla _XY=X(Y^i) rac{\partial }{\partial x^i}. ag {4.3} \end{equation}

If $M\subset \mathbb R^n$ is an embedded submanifold, the tangential acceleration of a curve is $\gamma ''{}^ op =\pi ^ op (\gamma '')$. For a local field $Y$ on $M$, extend it to $\widetilde Y$ near $M$ and define egin{equation} abla _v^ op Y=\pi ^ op ( ar abla _v\widetilde Y). ag {4.4} \end{equation} The projection is onto $T_pM$; independence of the extension is part of section 12. ↗ prop:normal-bundle

On an abstract manifold, velocity still has the coordinate-independent expression (1), but $\gamma '(t+h)$ and $\gamma '(t)$ lie in different tangent spaces, so their difference quotient is undefined. Coordinate expressions can therefore give incompatible accelerations (the unit circle has Cartesian acceleration $-\cos t\, \partial _x-\sin t\, \partial _y$ but polar expression $r''\partial _r+ heta ''\partial _ heta =0$). A connection supplies a coordinate-independent rule for comparing and differentiating such vectors.
